claims.statement: Reuters reported China's transport ministry count of 60 automated terminals and a target of 90 by 2030; Qianwan's 61 containers per crane-hour is a terminal-reported throughput claim, not a global verified capacity change.

Reuters described selected existing Chinese terminal operating-system installations overseas, citing a 2025 China Merchants Port filing, while separate LOGINK logistics-data platform ambitions had retreated by October 2026. Existing deployment is not evidence of new installations on November 10 or global coercive control.

Reuters commentary, using LSEG series, linked German weak wind and depressed Nordic and Danube hydro availability to rising gas generation and prices; this describes a simultaneous flexibility shortage rather than a newly commissioned or lost physical plant on Nov 10.

Reuters reported Brent at $90.18 and WTI $84.74 at 09:30 GMT amid declining perceived Iran escalation risk and oversupply expectations; the prices are market signals and do not independently verify Hormuz vessel throughput.
